title: Fascism or socialism: Rose's view of the future
summary: Rose sees a choice between fascism and socialism, describes socialist representation by industry, and expects capitalists to resist, ending in the failure of their own onslaught on labor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, what do you see taking its place, then?

What do I see for the future? Well, it depends upon who's victorious in the struggle. I see a choice between fascism and socialism. Hmm. But I do not see a chance for the continuation of capitalism. Hmm. And as between fascism and socialism, I will choose the socialism.

Because there are so many kinds. I just wondered what... There's only one kind of socialism, in fact. And that kind of socialism is a society that is organized in such a manner that the people that run the society have labor as their constituency. Hmm. Hmm. In other words, if you send a representative to Congress from a geographical district, he is basically responsible to represent the people in that district. In a socialist society, you would have a representative who came from the auto workers and a representative who came from the farm workers and so on. Hmm. That they would be represented by industry and that they would depend for their political lives upon the people that elected them, in fact. Hmm. Just as contemporary politicians are, except that the people would be different.

Hmm. Hmm. Hmm. So, you don't depend in politics on goodwill or idealists. You depend... And also, you never try to come to political conclusions on the basis of moral judgments. And nothing is more futile than for anybody to talk about how things should be. It's necessary to see how things are and determine how you're going to deal with those processes. Certainly, I can't imagine anybody relishing the idea of a revolution in progress. But any more than I can see anybody looking forward to a gallbladder operation.
But, in fact, there are certain things that are necessary, both in medicine and in life, which must be done for survival.
Certain things are inevitable, then. Yes. Now, this is going to occur through a natural process. It's not going to be a war for open warfare. Or...
Well, I can't see how it's going to be otherwise.
I mean, are you an orthodox Marxist in the sense you believe there's going to be an overthrow of a capitalist class?

Oh, yes. I can't imagine the American capitalist class or any capitalist class committing suicide as a class. I believe that the first job of every regime is to maintain itself in power. And I just can't see them peacefully surrendering it. However, I don't believe that it's going to succumb as a result of an onslaught from labor. I believe it is going to result as the failure of its own onslaught on labor. I can't see the working class taking the offensive or the initiative in creating a revolution.
